question.en: Critically examine the evolution of poverty estimation methodologies in India. How have these changes impacted the identification of the poor?
question.hi: Critically examine the evolution of poverty estimation methodologies in India. How have these changes impacted the identification of the poor?

introduction.en: Poverty estimation in India has evolved from a purely nutritional focus to a broader consumption-based framework to better reflect the changing economic landscape.
introduction.hi: Poverty estimation in India has evolved from a purely nutritional focus to a broader consumption-based framework to better reflect the changing economic landscape.

body.en: The Alagh Committee (1979) set the foundation using calorie norms. The Lakdawala Committee (1993) introduced state-specific lines. The Tendulkar Committee (2009) moved away from calorie norms to a uniform basket of goods, while the Rangarajan Committee (2014) further increased the poverty line to account for non-food expenditure. These shifts have expanded the definition of poverty but remain debated regarding their adequacy.

conclusion.en: While consumption-based metrics provide a baseline, India must integrate multidimensional indicators to address the complex nature of poverty effectively.
conclusion.hi: While consumption-based metrics provide a baseline, India must integrate multidimensional indicators to address the complex nature of poverty effectively.

valueAddition.en: The Tendulkar Committee poverty line was significantly lower than the Rangarajan Committee's, leading to debates on the 'true' number of poor.
